speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; can you tell me exactly how long you have had this sore and how it started? Also, have you noticed any fever, chills, or redness spreading around the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Necrotizing Fasciitis (suspected). The combination of a rapidly enlarging ulcerative lesion starting as an ant bite, coupled with significant immunocompromise (Crohn's on steroids, diabetes, hypertension), is highly concerning for a severe, life-threatening soft tissue infection. Given the urgency, I must immediately order blood work and imaging to assess the extent of tissue necrosis and sepsis. REQUEST TEST: CBC, BMP, Lactate, CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with contrast.
